latest_messages.headline: Midday: steady, no changes -- both stocks climbed, and JPMorgan's safety net auto-tightened to protect more of the gain.
latest_messages.body: I pulled our live account and re-checked both holdings. Risk first: nothing's falling toward its safety net, and JPMorgan's trailing stop (an auto-sell that follows the price up and only fires on a 10% drop from the peak) ratcheted higher on its own as the stock hit a new high today. Both stocks are strong: JPMorgan +9.5% and Deere +5.3% (Deere's best level with us). Because trailing stops climb automatically with each new high, our locked-in floor under JPMorgan rose today from about $323 to $327 a share -- more of the gain is now protected. No buys: no idea clears my 70+ quality bar, and I won't add fresh risk right before Friday's monthly jobs report. Deere's cushion improved a lot today, ~6.7% above its safety net (up from ~3.8% this morning). $101,822 total (+$628 / +0.62% today, +1.82% since our $100k start). The market is up ~+1.7% today, so we trail by ~1.1% intraday -- the price of ~75% cash on an up day. $75,894 cash (~75%), 0/3 weekly buys used. Full scorecard at the close.

latest_messages.headline: Open: no trades -- Texas Instruments came close but failed our safety check (scored 63, need 70).
latest_messages.body: The market opened up and we're +0.37% (+$370) with both holdings green. I dug into the one promising buy idea -- Texas Instruments (TXN, a big chip-maker) -- and passed. I sent a research assistant to double-check the story before risking a dime, and it didn't hold up: the earnings beat was real, but the 'wave' of Wall Street upgrades was smaller than it first looked (two of the named firms couldn't be verified), and -- the deciding factor -- the stock actually FELL ~5% on its own good news, sits 16-21% below its recent high, and company insiders have been heavily SELLING their shares. That trips our 'don't catch a falling knife' rule (signal #6, uptrend, fails). It scored ~63 on my 0-100 gauge; my buy-rule needs 70+, so it goes on the bench, not into the portfolio. I'd rather hold cash than force a mediocre trade -- that discipline is what protects us. Friday's monthly jobs report is a market-mover, so no rush to add risk. JPMorgan +7.1% and Deere +3.0%, both protected by trailing stops. ~$75,894 cash (~75%) still waiting for a GREAT setup, 0/3 weekly buys used.

latest_messages.headline: Week ending 7/31: -1.80% | SPY +1.07% | alpha -2.87% | grade C -- I need your call on our cash.
latest_messages.body: Honest week: we fell -1.80% while the market rose +1.07%, lagging by ~2.87% (2nd-worst week of the run). No mistake and no bad stock -- the miss is 100% structural: we held ~75% cash while the market climbed. Top win: Eli Lilly's safety net auto-sold for a +$627 profit and dodged its earnings risk (2nd trailing-stop win in a row). The pattern is now clear -- we beat the market on down weeks, trail it on up weeks, because we hold so much cash. Three up-weeks now stung. I will NOT lower our quality bar to force a trade, but I'm escalating a decision to you: (A) stay the course and hold cash until a great stock appears, or (B -- my lean) park some idle cash in an S&P 500 index fund so it keeps pace with the market instead of dragging, moving us from ~75% toward ~50-55% cash. Reply in the inbox; default is A (hold) if you don't. We're still +0.89% since our $100k start and +2.3% ahead of the market overall, but that lead halved from +5.2%. JPM (+6.7%) and DE (+0.5%) hold, both protected.
